FAQ

Before you call

Most ADUs are detached, a building of their own. They can also attach to the main house, from an open breezeway to a seamless addition. People use them for family, as a pool house, or as guest quarters. They are a direct way to add usable space on land you already own.

Stick-built means the base models can change, and we can also draw a custom ADU from scratch. Floor plans, room sizes, kitchen fixtures, cosmetic finishes. Many clients would rather be walked through the selections catalog, which is the short list of choices people tend to like.

Every city and HOA has its own rules. We walk the code with you: setbacks, how large the ADU can be, and how it has to be built to pass both the city and the HOA. Our free feasibility check gives you a first read before the property analysis.

Yes. A shell is the complete exterior plus rough plumbing, electrical, and framing. It is about 60% of a finished unit, for clients who want to handle the interior, or bring their own subcontractors.

Cash-out refinance, HELOC, renovation loans, and personal loans. The financing team helps you choose and secure one that fits.

It depends on size, finish level, site conditions and your city. Our pricing page shows illustrative ranges, and the free property analysis gives you an estimate for your lot.

A finished tiny home can be ready in 6 to 12 months. Permitting is a large part of the timeline and varies by city, so your project manager gives you a schedule once the location and plan are set.

Yes. We package the permit set and submit it. You do not have to become the permit runner.

It can. Some HOAs restrict or require approval for accessory buildings. We review your HOA rules as part of the analysis, and we recommend you ask for the covenants early.

Often, yes, but rental rules vary by city and by whether the rental is long-term or short-term. We can tell you what your city allows during the property analysis.

Water, sewer, electric and gas connections depend on your lot. We assess them during the property analysis so they are in the estimate and not a surprise later.

New construction can change a property's assessed value. Rules differ by county, so ask your county assessor or tax advisor. We are not tax advisors.

No. A project manager is your point of contact and keeps you updated on progress.

A 1-year workmanship warranty, plus the manufacturer warranties that come with the materials. See the warranty page for details.
